label: Figure 5
title: Nine stages, four groups of gates and eight failure patterns
caption: The spine of the guide drawn as one picture: the nine lifecycle stages in order, the four groups of gates that bind them (the contract and customer through the labor category, the key-personnel clause and the rate ceiling [98](#cite:98) [197](#cite:197); the law through the Uniform Guidelines and the hiring statutes [30](#cite:30); the government through eligibility, sponsorship and vetting [119](#cite:119); the law again through the repayment, noncompete, no-poach and notice rules [187](#cite:187) [191](#cite:191)), and the eight observed failure patterns placed at the stage where each is seen. This is a conceptual figure: it shows how the records are organised, not any one firm's process.
how_to_read: Follow the middle row left to right from planning an opening to handing a role over. The boxes above and below the row are the rules that bind the stages they connect to; a thicker connection means more of that stage's gates belong to the group. The boxes at the bottom are the failure points the pathfinder starts from: pick the one you are seeing and the stage it points at is where the constraints to read are.

explain.text: The nine stages the selection and turnover literatures use, as the stage records state them; each record says who decides what at that stage.
A grouping of the gate records for the picture only; each gate record names its governing text.
The seven failure points from the original matrix, re-derived from the evidence, plus the customer-rejection pattern; each pattern record lists the constraints it points at in order of the evidence.

source: The drawing is the builder's own, built from the stage, gate and pattern records; the gate groupings are a simplification for the picture and the records themselves are the authority.
